name: Arabic (Hindu–Arabic) Numerals
morphology: Digits (0–9) represent values multiplied by powers of ten according to position.
hierarchy: Position determines magnitude: ones (10^0), tens (10^1), hundreds (10^2), and so on.
context: The Hindu–Arabic numeral system originated in India and was later transmitted to the Islamic world and Europe. It is now the global standard.
rules: Base-10 positional system where each digit represents a power of 10 depending on its position.
Digits range from 0 to 9 and have no internal additive or multiplicative roles.
Numbers are read left to right from the highest position.
